idea: Koubo is an agent skill that turns one photo and one sentence into a finished talking-head video: script, lip-synced clips, captions, packaging, all driven by a coding agent.

claims.text: Koubo turns one photo and one sentence into a finished talking-head video with script, lip-synced presenter, captions and packaging.
The pipeline splits the script into segments of 15 seconds or less, generates them through Renoise MCP, then whisper-checks every segment against the script.
It ships 5 editing styles and 48 packaging components measured frame by frame from 25 videos by top creators.
The 27-second demo ad cost 482 Renoise credits, and Renoise login happens in the browser with no API key.
The text-behind-presenter effect uses Apple Vision and needs macOS; the rest is cross-platform.
The repo is MIT licensed, and every demo video is labelled as performed by an AI digital human.

scenes.headline: THIS PRESENTER IS *NOT REAL*
scenes.say: This sales ad has no real presenter in it. The only input was one photo and one sentence.

scenes.heading: ONE SKILL RUNS *ALL OF IT*
scenes.say: It is an agent skill called Koubo. Your coding agent writes the script, renders every segment through Renoise, then whisper checks each line and cuts the video in Remotion.
Five styles ship with it: a finance explainer, a launch breakdown, a tutorial, and shows with two hosts, plus forty-eight packaging tricks taken from top creators.

scenes.heading: THE *CATCH*
cons: Renoise balance: 482 for the demo ad
scenes.say: The catch: no camera or studio, and whisper checks every line, but generation burns your Renoise balance, four hundred eighty-two for that demo ad, and the text-behind trick needs macOS.
Would you put an AI presenter on your channel? Comment koubo and I will pin the repo, free and open source.
